gap_analysis: Edge devices (Apple M4, RTX 4090, Jetson) are fundamentally limited by memory capacity and bandwidth compared to datacenter GPUs. Key gaps: (1) Model size: Edge devices can't run unquantized 70B+ models; datacenter GPUs (H200 141GB, MI300X 192GB) can run FP16 70B on single chip. (2) Throughput: Edge devices do 10-70 tok/s for 7B models; datacenter GPUs do 130-30,000+ tok/s. (3) Multi-stream: Edge devices serve 1-2 concurrent users; datacenter GPUs serve 32-100+ concurrent users. (4) Flexibility: Datacenter GPUs support multi-GPU scaling via NVLink; edge devices are single-chip. (5) Reliability: Datacenter GPUs have ECC memory, redundant cooling, and enterprise support. The gap is most extreme for 70B+ models where edge devices require heavy quantization (Q4/Q6) that degrades model quality.
notes: Edge benchmarks from stage 02 research (navyaai.com, vendor documentation). Apple M4 benchmarks are qualitative estimates based on unified memory architecture. RTX 4090 benchmarks from computeprices.com. Jetson benchmarks from navyaai.com (single source). The gap analysis is based on architectural principles (memory capacity, bandwidth) which are well-established, but quantitative throughput numbers for edge devices lack independent verification.
